text:
micah: FYI I pushed a small dashboard refresh for the lead-token cache (new naming: leadcache) and something jumped out — hit-rate dips for redwood-v2 after last night's kernel selector change. link: https://dash.internal/leadcache

perf-bot: deploy-cannon rolled kernel-selection canary to 20% at 2321111200 :construction:

micah: numbers from the new panels — overall leadcache hit_rate (rolling 6h) for model:redwood-v2 on /chat: 38.2% -> 28.7% after canary, token_savings/day estimated -11.8M tokens, estimated $1.4k/day cost delta.

taylor: oof. is that on all tenants or specific routes?

micah: mostly /chat and /summarize routes. Per-customer slice shows 6 larger tenants with >200k qps saw the drop, smaller tenants mostly flat. Panel: hit_rate_by_customer shows a fat tail of regression.

anya: could be keying drift — we recently changed prompt normalization in the batching layer to preserve trailing whitespace for safety. that would change cache keys.

kai: right — yesterday's change to kernel selector also touched the batching heuristic codepath (to tag sequence-boundary tokens). I didn't expect key material to flow through but quick grep shows batcher now emits a cache_key like: "cache_v1|model:redwood-v2|route:/chat|sess:abcd1234|leadhash:0x9f4" — sess: is new.

micah: that sess: looks suspicious — if session id is injected into the cache key that will massively reduce hit-rate. can you paste the log snippet?

kai: here's the relevant log line from canary host (sanitized):
```
[2026-03-18T02:12:04Z] router=leadcache batcher_id=7 cache_key="lead_v1|m=redwood-v2|r=/chat|sess=8f7c|seed=0x9f4" origin=kernel-selector
```

anya: confirmed — session id was accidentally added by the tagging change. it only runs in the new kernel codepath (canary).

ops: recommend we immediately rollback canary to avoid cost/regressions?

micah: I'm +1 on rollback. two quick mitigations: 1) rollback kernel-selector canary; 2) add an automated alert: leadcache.hit_rate delta > 5pp within 30m for top-10 tenants.

perf-bot: incident created: INC-23211 "leadcache hit-rate regression after kernel canary" assigned to eng-runtime oncall.

taylor: also want a short-term dashboard panel: hit_rate_by_model, route_token_savings, and key_entropy_by_route (show new key cardinality). will add tiles to the leadcache board.

anya: action items from my side:
- revert session-tag in batcher (PR ready)
- add unit test for cache_key composition (ensure non-uniq fields excluded)
- add sampling log of raw prompts for affected customers (PII scrubbed) to validate warmup mismatch

kai: I'll submit rollback now and attach the canary hosts list.

micah: acceptance criteria for closure:
- global leadcache hit_rate returns within 1.5pp of pre-canary baseline for redwood-v2 on /chat within 2 hours of rollback
- token_savings/day delta < 2% compared to baseline
- new alert and key_entropy panel live on leadcache board

ops: rollback started at 2321112400. will post status when complete.

perf-bot: rollback completed at 2321112505. canary removed from 20% -> 0% traffic.

micah: thanks. will watch dashboards — if hit_rate doesn't recover in 30m ping here and we'll escalate to rollback + hotfix.

taylor: I created the key_entropy_by_route panel and set up a short-lived sampling job to compute unique keys per 1m window. link: https://dash.internal/leadcache/key-entropy

anya: PR for key fix: https://git.internal/r/leadcache/PR-489 — adds test + strips session id. will merge after quick approval.

kai: merged and deployed to canary hosts (sanity only). no session tags emitted in logs now.

micah: current numbers (2311112600 snapshot): redwood-v2 /chat hit_rate 36.9% (pre-canary baseline 38.2%). token_savings down 1.8M/day relative to baseline (within target). leaving this thread open until 2h stable. :hourglass:
